title: Locally hosted LLM
body:
Hi,

How would one go about connecting mcp-playwright to a locally hosted LLM?

At my company we have huge concerns around security and we have our own locally hosted LLM.

Does mcp-playwright only integrate with Claude because of its mcp integration and if so, is it possible to have Claude hosted locally?
author: ajsteenkamp

comments.body: Sorry its not an issue and hence closing it !

@ajsteenkamp I think you're looking at this backwards.
The MCP server is just a generic server.  It doesn't "know" about Claude or Cline or any other client using it.  It just so happens that Claude Desktop can use the MCP Server, but so can VSCode + Cline or Cursor, or Windsurf, or a few other LLM chat programs (I lost track of the alternatives).
I think an LLM chat program that supports MCP servers and custom LLM configuration is what you are looking for.  Maybe OpenWebUI or GPT4ALL or something like that?  They're all adding features so fast, I don't know which you'd be looking for.
Worst case scenario, you could install VSCode with the Cline plugin, add the MCP server to Cline, point Cline to a local LLM, and then just chat through VS Code!  Kinda hacky, but it'd work.

title: feat: Added jest and some tests
body: @executeautomation  This PR adds jest, some tests and a GitHub Action. It has been created using Cline with MCP servers like this one ;-)
author: kfern

comments.body: Can you please add the test for new tools added in past couple of days, it will be helpful @kfern . Thanks for the tests, they are awesome, I love it too !

> Can you please add the test for new tools added in past couple of days, it will be helpful @kfern . Thanks for the tests, they are awesome, I love it too !

Hi @executeautomation. Thanks :-)

I have a problem with playwright_console_logs.

The `playwright_console_logs` tool is currently incorrectly included in the `BROWSER_TOOLS` array in `src/tools.ts`. This classification suggests that `playwright_console_logs` requires a browser instance to function, which is not the case.

The `playwright_console_logs` tool retrieves and filters console logs that are already stored in memory. Launching a browser instance for this tool is unnecessary and interferes with tests that are designed to run without a browser.

To resolve this issue, we need to remove `playwright_console_logs` from the `BROWSER_TOOLS` array in `src/tools.ts`. This will correctly classify the tool as not requiring a browser instance.

The incorrect classification is located in `src/tools.ts` in the `BROWSER_TOOLS` array:

```typescript
// Browser-requiring tools for conditional browser launch
export const BROWSER_TOOLS = [
  "playwright_navigate",
  "playwright_screenshot",
  "playwright_click",
  "playwright_iframe_click",
  "playwright_fill",
  "playwright_select",
  "playwright_hover",
  "playwright_evaluate",
  "playwright_console_logs", // <-- Incorrectly included here
  "playwright_close",
];
```
Do you know if there was a specific reason why playwright_console_logs is included in BROWSER_TOOLS? Understanding the original intent might reveal if there are any edge cases we need to consider.

On the other hand, I think we can merge these tests and add new ones later.
You are correct, we can remove the playwright_console_logs, it's irrelevant in this context, will make the fix now. Thanks for bringing it up !

title: Allow screenshots to be saved to disk
body:
# Overview

This PR extends the screenshot functionality in MCP Playwright by adding support for file storage options and an option to disable base64 encoding.

## Changes

- Added new screenshot parameters:
  - storeBase64 - Option to store screenshot in base64 format (default: true)
  - savePng - Option to save screenshot as PNG file (default: false)
  - downloadsDir - Custom downloads directory path (defaults to user's Downloads folder)

## Important Note
The downloadsDir parameter requires write permissions to be properly configured in the server. Ensure the specified directory is in the allowed write paths before using this feature.

## Example Usage
```
// Store as base64 only
{
  name: "screenshot-name",
  storeBase64: true
}

// Save as PNG file only
{
  name: "screenshot-name",
  savePng: true,
  storeBase64: false,
  downloadsDir: "/custom/path"  // optional
}
```
